fact: The dashboard is now interactive AND legible, in two measured steps. (1) INPUT: staged evdev.ko + psmouse.ko into the RAM image mods[] (24 modules; atkbd built-in), turning enumerated input into /dev/input/event* -- boot log reads 'DASHBOARD RENDERER: 2 input device(s)'. New src/input.rs reads the 24-byte struct input_event directly (no crate, mirroring the trm_wifi FFI pattern), moves a crosshair on REL/ABS and arrow keys, and hit-tests a click against the SAME panel_rects() that draw() uses so the click target cannot disagree with the screen. PROVEN by pixel analysis: injected mouse REL moved the crosshair to (955,226) and keyboard KEY_DOWN+KEY_LEFT to (600,440) -- 17 text-colored pixels at each spot, exactly the 9px crosshair. (2) TEXT: swapped the 5x7 bitmap font for fontdue (2-crate chain fontdue->ttf-parser, both pure Rust no_std, no system deps) rasterizing an embedded DejaVu Sans Mono TTF (Bitstream Vera, 343,140 B), per-pixel coverage blended so glyphs anti-alias. PROVEN: the title 'TRM SWARM OS' renders centered in the cyan rail (rows 8-25 of the 36px rail, unclipped) and the four panel heads + value lines are pixel-positioned correctly. One real bug found and fixed: fontdue's Metrics.ymin is the glyph's BOTTOM edge (negative = below baseline), not the top, so the first pass drew every line one line low and clipped the title at the rail edge -- corrected placement is baseline - ymin - height + row.
not_claimed: The literal 'selected panel' log line was not captured in QEMU because an injected button down+up coalesces at the PS/2 controller (cursor motion proves the EV_KEY read path; the button-code dispatch confirms on metal). The metal stick E: is still the pre-input build -- restage is the remaining step. Glyph legibility was confirmed as positioned anti-aliased pixels (title rows 8-25, heads y=52/412, values y=103/463), not by an image-capable model reading the text.
